text: I began studying carvings after assisting Kaladatta with monument maintenance.
He sees wear and repair cycles. I see repeating symbols.
Certain carvings appear in multiple unrelated locations.
These repetitions are too consistent to be decorative.
The temple Song contains recurring structural phrases.
Some of these phrases match stone markings.
Vasu has confirmed variations in older ritual transcripts.
The variations may indicate a lost original sequence.
Senaka tells stories containing fragments of identical phrasing patterns.
These patterns may have drifted through oral transmission.
Kaladatta believes differences in carvings are repair-based.
I believe some repairs are actually reinterpretations.
The monument base contains repeated geometric motifs that do not serve structural purposes.
I have cataloged over a hundred variations of the same symbol cluster.
No one agrees on what they mean.
That disagreement itself may be meaningful.
After the Agnikanda, certain inscriptions were damaged selectively.
Not randomly.
Some patterns were erased more thoroughly than others.
That suggests intent or selective preservation.
Tarala once described carvings she saw in the forest that matched monument patterns.
She did not realize their significance.
Chapala has found physical routes that align with symbolic sequences I have mapped.
This is unlikely to be coincidence.
The Song may not be a song at all in its original form.
It may be a structured encoding system.
Vasu disagrees with me on this.
But he continues to document variations with me.
I believe we are reconstructing something that was deliberately fragmented.
I do not yet know why.
